prompt.context: One of the many functions of the New York State Health Commission is to coordinate organ donation amongst the state's many hospitals. In recent years the demand for organs has been greater than the supply. As a result, many patients die each year because there are not enough organ donations. The Health Commission has hired McKinsey to help it determine how to increase the number of annual organ donations in New York. For the purposes of this case, assume that only New York residents are involved as donors and recipients.
prompt.question: How can the New York State Health Commission increase the number of annual organ donations in New York?

clarifying_info.q: How does organ harvesting work in New York?
clarifying_info.a: In New York, organs will be harvested from terminally ill or injured patients just before death only if they are a registered organ donor or if the hospital receives permission from the next of kin.

clarifying_info.q: How do people register as organ donors?
clarifying_info.a: New York residents may choose to register as organ donors when they apply for a driver's license.

exhibits.title: Organ Donor Segmentation Data
exhibits.shows: A table showing Registered Donors and Population figures (in millions) broken down by four demographic segments: Caucasian, African-American, Hispanic, and Other.

framework: Identify the key factors/drivers of organ donations using a structured equation: (Terminal patients x % Registered donors x organs/donor) + (Terminal patients x % Not registered x % Family consent x organs/donor) = organs donated
Quantify the required registration rate to meet demand (math/quantification)
Brainstorm ways to increase the number of registered donors: benchmarking, segmentation, marketing, distribution
Analyze segmentation data to identify the highest-opportunity target demographic
Develop targeted tactics for the chosen segment

questions.prompt: What are the factors and drivers that determine the number of organs donated in New York each year?
questions.guidance: A good answer frames the problem as an equation: (Terminal patients x % Registered donors x organs/donor) + (Terminal patients x % Not registered x % Family consent x organs/donor) = organs donated. Should identify 3-4 drivers for each factor. A great answer notes that only two factors are truly influenceable: the rate of registered donors and the rate of family consent. Drivers: terminal patients (population size, age, lifespan, medical technology, accident rates); % registered (awareness, ease of registration, opt-in vs opt-out, religious beliefs); % family consent (awareness, religious beliefs, doctor communication, assurance of death confirmation); organs per donor (average number of healthy usable organs).

questions.prompt: The team has decided to focus on increasing registered donors and is specifically interested in kidney donations. The Health Commission needs 9,200 kidneys per year. What percent of New Yorkers need to be registered donors to achieve this? (Population: 10 million; % terminally ill/injured per year: 0.1%; % family consent: 10%)
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up and solve algebraically. Key insight: 9,200 kidneys / 2 kidneys per person = 4,600 donors needed. RD = percent registered donors. Must account for both registered donors and non-registered donors whose families consent. A great answer interprets the 40% result as plausible based on personal experience.

math.setup: Let RD = percent of New Yorkers who are registered donors. Total donors needed = 9,200 / 2 = 4,600 (two kidneys per person). Equation: (10,000,000 x 0.001 x RD) + (10,000,000 x 0.001 x 0.10 x (1-RD)) = 4,600
math.answer: 40% of New Yorkers must be registered donors

questions.prompt: What are all of the things the Health Commission should consider doing to increase the number of registered donors?
questions.guidance: Answer should be MECE with discrete categories and multiple items within each. Strong answer covers: (1) Benchmarking - internal to identify strengths, external of other states/countries for new ideas; (2) Segmentation - identify strong segments to cultivate and underserved segments to develop; (3) Marketing communications - test messaging and channels (TV, radio, online, direct mail, word-of-mouth), increase awareness of program benefits and safeguards; (4) Distribution/registration optimization - add new touchpoints (doctors, hospitals), consider opt-out default instead of opt-in.

questions.prompt: The team conducted a customer segmentation. Review the data handout and draw initial conclusions. Which segment represents the best opportunity to increase registered donors?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate penetration rates. Caucasian 2.6/5.5=47% - largest absolute upside (2.9M potential new) but already highly penetrated. African-American 0.075/1.5=5% - very low penetration but small population (1.5M). Hispanic 0.25/2.5=10% - low penetration and large population, best combination. A good answer selects a target with clear reasoning; Hispanic is the strongest choice but logic matters more than the specific answer. Risks for Hispanic: language barrier, cultural differences.

math.setup: Calculate penetration rate = Registered Donors / Population for each segment
math.answer: Hispanic segment offers best opportunity: low 10% penetration rate combined with large population of 2.5M, yielding 2.25M potential new registrants

questions.prompt: The team has decided to focus on increasing registration among Hispanics. What are some things we can do to increase registrations?
questions.guidance: This question tests creativity. No single correct answer. Expect ideas such as: community outreach programs, Spanish-language marketing materials and registration forms, partnering with Hispanic community organizations and churches, mobile registration vans in Hispanic neighborhoods, leveraging Hispanic media (Univision, Spanish radio), partnering with Hispanic doctors and healthcare workers as trusted messengers, culturally sensitive messaging addressing religious concerns, incentive programs, social media campaigns. Interviewer should push with 'What else?' to test depth and response to pressure.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some things we can do to increase organ donor registrations among Hispanics?

categories.name: Community Outreach
ideas: Partner with Hispanic community organizations and churches
Host registration events in Hispanic neighborhoods
Mobile registration vans in Hispanic communities

categories.name: Marketing and Communications
ideas: Spanish-language marketing materials and registration forms
Advertise on Hispanic media (Univision, Telemundo, Spanish radio)
Social media campaigns targeting Hispanic users
Culturally sensitive messaging addressing religious and cultural concerns

categories.name: Distribution and Registration Access
ideas: Add registration touchpoints at clinics and hospitals serving Hispanic populations
Partner with Hispanic grocery stores and community centers
Enable registration at Hispanic community events

categories.name: Trusted Messengers
ideas: Hispanic doctors and healthcare workers as advocates
Endorsements from Hispanic celebrities or community leaders

categories.name: Policy and Process
ideas: Simplify the registration form in Spanish
Offer incentives or recognition for registration

recommendation: Focus short-term efforts on the Hispanic segment, which has the lowest penetration (10%) among large demographic groups and represents 2.25M potential new registrants
Launch a targeted Spanish-language outreach and registration campaign leveraging community organizations, Hispanic media, and mobile registration units in Hispanic neighborhoods
Add registration touchpoints at healthcare facilities serving Hispanic communities to capture high-intent moments
risks: Language and cultural barriers may slow adoption and require significant investment in culturally tailored materials
Religious or cultural beliefs around organ donation in some Hispanic communities may limit registration rates
Community trust in the healthcare system may be low and require sustained relationship-building before results materialize
next_steps: Conduct benchmarking of other states or countries with high Hispanic registration rates
Pilot 2-3 marketing channels (Spanish TV, community outreach, mobile vans) and measure registration lift
Identify and engage key community and religious leaders as program ambassadors
